title: AcceleratorRegistry
description: The JSON that ai-hwaccel prints by default (and with --json): detected accelerators, detection warnings and system I/O. schema_version 6. Written by registry_to_json in src/json_out.cyr. The other JSON outputs are under $defs: Summary (--summary), ShardingPlan (--plan), TrainingMemory (--train) and CostReport (--cost --json). Every key in an object is listed; optional keys are omitted, never null, when a value is unknown or does not apply. String values are JSON-escaped (RFC 8259) since 2.5.5: a quote, backslash or control byte in a device name, a tool's output or the --cost argument no longer breaks the document.

schema_version.description: Bumped whenever the format gains or changes keys. 6 since 2.3.28 (shared_memory_bytes).

profiles.description: One profile per detected device, the CPU first. A device that two backends report is listed once (since 2.4.0).

warnings.description: Names of the vendor tools that were not found or failed (for example "nvidia-smi"), one per attempt. Omitted when there are none.

system_io.description: Interconnects, storage and the runtime environment (since schema v4).

AcceleratorProfile.description: One device. profile_from_json (src/json_out.cyr) reads it back: since 2.5.5 a key holding another type than the one below (null, a string, a float) reads as absent, and a value outside the ranges below makes it refuse the profile, as malformed JSON does.

accelerator.description: Display name of the accelerator type. "Unknown" only when a consumer re-serializes a profile read back with an accel_type_id this build does not know.

accel_type_id.description: The accelerator type as a number, the authoritative tag when a profile is read back (profile_from_json). This build writes 0..19; reading back, it keeps a higher id (a newer producer's type) and refuses a negative one.

device_id.description: Index within the backend, at most 1024 (CMD_MAX_DEVICE_ID, the bound every tool parser applies).

memory_bytes.description: Memory the device can use. For a device on system RAM this includes the shared part below. At most 16 TiB (17592186044416) for an accelerator, the tool parsers' bound, except a TPU, whose memory may reach tpu_chips x 95 GiB (v5p HBM), and 1 PiB (1125899906842624) for the CPU profile's system RAM.

family.description: "Unknown" only for a re-serialized profile whose accel_type_id this build does not know.

compute_capability.description: CUDA compute capability ("8.9"), or the ROCm gfx target.

memory_used_bytes.description: At most memory_bytes' bound for the type.

memory_free_bytes.description: At most memory_bytes' bound for the type.

shared_memory_bytes.description: The part of memory_bytes that is system RAM, which the CPU profile already counts: all of it for Apple Silicon, the client NPUs and integrated GPUs on system RAM; 480 GiB on a GH200. At most memory_bytes. Never on the CPU profile: profile_from_json ignores it there and reads 0 as absent. Absent, the reader derives it from the type (all of memory_bytes on a system-memory type, else none). Since schema v6.

state.description: For InfiniBand and RoCE, the port state number sysfs reports (4 is ACTIVE); 4 for an NVSwitch; 0 when unknown, as for the other kinds.

Summary.description: ai-hwaccel --summary (registry_to_summary_json). Totals count system RAM once.

fits.description: Whether every shard fits the memory of the device it names. false when nothing holds the model: the CPU fallback ('None' on the CPU) asks for more than the CPU's memory, or no device is available ('Data Parallel', no shards). Added in 2.5.5.

est_tokens_per_sec_x1000.description: Estimated throughput, tokens/s x 1000. Omitted when unknown.

TrainingMemory.description: ai-hwaccel --train <model> [--method <m>] (training_to_json). Each figure twice: bytes, and GiB x 1000.
